records.claim_summary: Reality models separate fill, fee, slippage, settlement, portfolio, and capacity assumptions for more realistic backtests.
Fill models determine fill price and quantity and can incorporate spread and slippage effects.
Slippage models capture the difference between expected and actual fill prices.
Settlement models simulate whether trade proceeds are immediately or later available.
Suitable QuadraticProgram instances can be converted to Ising Hamiltonians and solved with SamplingVQE, QAOA, or a classical exact comparator.
Dimod model classes encode Ising and QUBO/BQM structures consumed by D-Wave samplers.
Samplers accept quadratic model formats such as BQM and CQM and return variable assignments.
Tasks are organized in DAGs with explicit upstream and downstream dependencies.
Benjamini-Hochberg introduces a sequential procedure for controlling false discovery rate under multiple testing.
Deflated Sharpe Ratio adjusts for selection bias under multiple testing and non-normal returns.
Almgren-Chriss frames optimal execution as a cost and risk tradeoff with temporary and permanent market impact.
